units.title: Skills and understanding common to all areas of study

topics.title: Skills and understanding common to all areas of study

subtopics.title: Recording and organising information

outcomes.text: Record their own experiences and observations from first-hand and secondary resources and personal research.
Collect, record and respond to visual information using a range of techniques.
Select, give context to and organise the information they collect in a coherent way.
Effectively use a wide range of resources and use the information to develop their practice.

subtopics.title: Investigating, making and reflecting

outcomes.text: Make personal investigations.
Apply a range of skills to produce art and design work.
Evaluate their own work, review and edit.
Reflect, refine and adapt.

subtopics.title: What painting and related media involves

outcomes.text: Develop knowledge and skills in a broad range of media, processes and techniques; demonstrate a personal response through painting and related media, working to a theme, starting point or brief, and show the ability to consider artistic constraints and problems, considering traditional, contemporary and emerging techniques and approaches.
Work in one or more of the following: painting; drawing; assemblage/collage; printmaking; mixed media.

subtopics.title: Researching and developing painting and related media work

outcomes.text: Carry out visual research, using direct observation (first-hand) and secondary sources, and record observations, experiences and ideas in appropriate ways.
Explore and experiment with a wide range of different media (including recycled materials), techniques and processes.
Carry out in-depth research into artists, designers and cultural influences to inform the development of their ideas.
Select, review and refine their work throughout the whole process to produce a personal and resolved response.

subtopics.title: Painting and related media skills and techniques

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to use appropriate materials, including recycled material, and techniques to communicate their intention effectively.
Demonstrate an understanding of form, perspective and scale.
Demonstrate the ability to create images with consideration for space, balance and colour relationships.
Demonstrate effective use of a few appropriate skills such as tonal drawing, pen and ink, pastels, painting, printmaking, collage.
Demonstrate the ability to respond to a theme or given starting point.

subtopics.title: Knowledge and understanding of painting and related media

outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of appropriate materials, processes, technologies and resources.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how painting and related media can be used to communicate ideas and observations.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of social and cultural factors.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of relevant painting and related media genres, styles and techniques used by artists, past and present.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of intention, research, realisation and reflection to the artistic process.

subtopics.title: What graphic communication involves

outcomes.text: Develop knowledge and skills in a broad range of media, processes and techniques; demonstrate visual meaning through graphic communication, working to a theme, starting point or brief and considering design constraints and problems, considering traditional, contemporary and emerging techniques and approaches.
Work in one or more of the following: illustration; printmaking; packaging design; advertising; typography.

subtopics.title: Researching and developing graphic communication work

outcomes.text: Carry out visual research, using direct observation (first-hand) and secondary sources, and record observations, experiences and ideas in appropriate ways.
Explore and experiment with a wide range of different media, techniques and processes such as print media, collage, pencils, inks and paper construction.
Show an awareness of current and historical design processes and concepts.
Explore the relationship between image and text, the use of colour composition, problem-solving and communication to develop ideas.
Select, review and refine their work throughout the whole process to produce a personal and resolved response.

subtopics.title: Graphic communication skills and techniques

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to use appropriate materials, including recycled, and techniques to communicate their intention effectively.
Demonstrate an understanding of perspective, scale and colour.
Demonstrate the ability to create designs with consideration for space, balance and colour relationships.
Demonstrate effective use of a few appropriate skills such as drawing, photography, photo editing, printmaking, typography and lettering, product design and package construction.
Demonstrate the ability to respond to a theme, starting point or design brief.
Demonstrate an awareness of the intended audience.

subtopics.title: Knowledge and understanding of graphic communication

outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of appropriate materials, processes, technologies and resources.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how graphic design can be used to communicate ideas and observations.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of social and cultural factors in the making, exhibiting and viewing of work.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of relevant graphic communication styles and techniques used by designers, past and present.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of intention, research, realisation and reflection to the graphic design process.

subtopics.title: What three-dimensional design involves

outcomes.text: Develop knowledge and skills in a broad range of media, processes and techniques; demonstrate understanding of the development of designs for a three-dimensional outcome, working to a theme or brief and considering design constraints and problems, considering traditional, contemporary and emerging techniques and approaches.

Work in one or more of the following: sculpture/ceramics; product design; architectural: interior design/set design; craft design: metalwork, papercrafts and woodwork; jewellery and fashion accessories.

subtopics.title: Researching and developing three-dimensional design work

outcomes.text: Carry out visual research, using direct observation (first-hand) and secondary sources, and record observations, experiences and ideas in appropriate ways to show clear evidence of the development of their ideas.

Explore and experiment with a wide range of different media, techniques and processes such as clay, plaster, cardboard, metal, string and tape and recycled material to develop maquettes for further development.
Carry out in-depth research into images and resources related to three-dimensional design, which reference a range of cultural, social and local contexts.
Explore form, function and surface using models, samples, materials exploration and technical notes to develop their ideas.
Select, review and refine their work throughout the whole process to plan and produce a personal and resolved response.

subtopics.title: Three-dimensional design skills and techniques

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to use appropriate materials and techniques to communicate their intention effectively.
Demonstrate an understanding of form, structure and scale.
Demonstrate the ability to create designs with consideration of texture, shape, colour and movement.
Demonstrate effective use of a few appropriate specialist working processes and equipment such as kilns, CAD, laser cutters and hand tools.
Demonstrate the ability to respond to a theme or given starting point or brief.
Demonstrate consideration of the intended audience for the work.

subtopics.title: Knowledge and understanding of three-dimensional design

outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of appropriate materials, processes, technologies and resources.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how three-dimensional design can be used to communicate ideas.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of social and cultural factors in the making, exhibiting and viewing of work.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of relevant genres, styles and techniques used by artists and designers, past and present.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of intention, research, realisation and reflection to the three-dimensional design process.

subtopics.title: What textiles and fashion involves

outcomes.text: Develop knowledge and skills in a broad range of media, processes and techniques; demonstrate understanding of the development of designs for a textiles or fashion outcome, working to a theme, starting point or brief and considering design constraints and problems, considering traditional, contemporary and emerging techniques and approaches.
Work in one or more of the following: fashion design and/or illustration; costume design; screen printing; batik; surface pattern.

subtopics.title: Researching and developing textiles and fashion work

outcomes.text: Carry out visual research, using direct observation (first-hand) and secondary sources, and record observations, experiences and ideas in appropriate ways to show clear evidence of the development of their ideas.

Explore and experiment with a wide range of different media, techniques and processes such as pencil, paint, inks, marker pens, pastels, fabric swatches, recycled materials, samples, mock-ups and toiles, fabric dyeing, printing and hand- and machine-embroidery.
Develop an understanding of material, trends, manufacturing, local crafts and cultural factors relating to textiles and fashion, different types of fabric, manipulation and surface treatments.
Select, review and refine their work throughout the process to produce a personal and resolved response, which may include fashion illustrations, hand-made costumes or contemporary textile designs.

subtopics.title: Textiles and fashion skills and techniques

outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to use appropriate materials and techniques to communicate their intention effectively.
Demonstrate an understanding of form, function and colour relationships within the design process.
Demonstrate the ability to create designs with consideration of texture, pattern and shape.

Demonstrate effective use of a few appropriate specialist working processes and equipment such as fabric construction, dyeing and printing; screen and mono printing; batik; embroidery and machine stitching.
Demonstrate the ability to respond to a theme, starting point or brief.
Demonstrate consideration of the intended audience for the work.

subtopics.title: Knowledge and understanding of textiles and fashion

outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of appropriate materials, processes, technologies and resources.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how textiles and fashion design can be used to communicate ideas.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of social and cultural factors in the making, exhibiting and viewing of work.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of relevant textile and fashion genres, styles and techniques used by designers, past and present.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of intention, research, realisation and reflection to the textile and fashion design process.

subtopics.title: What photography involves

outcomes.text: Develop knowledge of skills and processes relevant to photography; understand formal elements, animation, film or game design such as using narrative and visual language to create meaning, and using composition and planning layouts (drawing skills for animation could include character development, background and storyboards); use appropriate specialist technical language and support creative work with technical notes and records.

Work in one or more of the following: traditional film photography; digital photography; camera-less photography; animation: hand-drawn or computer-aided or a combination; photomontage or photocollage.

subtopics.title: Researching and developing photography work

outcomes.text: Carry out visual research, using direct observation (first-hand) and secondary sources, and record observations, experiences and ideas in appropriate ways to show clear evidence of the development of their ideas.
Explore and experiment with techniques relevant to photography such as depth of field, lighting and exposure, aperture/shutter speed, angle and view-point/composition, framing and editing.

Explore and experiment with different photographic media and processes such as abstracting, documenting, developing and printing of films, pin-hole camera, photograms, multiple exposure, photosensitive surfaces and alternative print processes, image scanning and manipulation and digital manipulation.
For animation, film and game design, explore relevant media and processes such as hand-drawn, stop motion or digital animation.
Select, review and refine their work throughout the process to produce a personal response.

subtopics.title: Photography skills and techniques

outcomes.text: Demonstrate storyboarding and image-making through photography, model-making, drawing and/or illustration.
Demonstrate an understanding of the conventions of photography and genres such as portrait, landscape and documentary.
Demonstrate the ability to respond to a theme or brief.
Demonstrate consideration of the intended audience for the work.

subtopics.title: Knowledge and understanding of photography

outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of different types and genres of photography and/or animation.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of appropriate materials, processes, technologies and resources.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the importance of intention, research, realisation and reflection to the relevant processes.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of a range of relevant artists, photographers or animators.
